attribute-definition.description: Turn the Gameball Integration on or off. Also requires the "gameball.http.api.cred" Service Credential (Administration > Operations > Services > Service Credentials) to be filled in with a valid API Key (User ID) and Secret Key (Password).

attribute-definition.display-name: Exclude Gift Certificate Tender from Gameball totalPaid
attribute-definition.description: When enabled (the default), the portion of an order paid for with a Gift Certificate is subtracted from the totalPaid amount reported to Gameball, so points are not awarded on gift-certificate-funded spend.

Writes one INFO line to the custom Gameball log for every customer upsert the storefront sends or deliberately skips. This is the only way an operator can confirm that exactly one Gameball customer upsert is sent per registration and per profile save - count the "upsert sent" lines sharing one sfccRequestId. Turning it off silences the success lines, the skip lines AND the transient-failure warnings (rate limit, service timeout, Gameball-side 5xx), which means a Gameball outage stops appearing in the log at all; only permanent errors are written regardless of this setting. Leave it on unless log volume forces otherwise.

Writes DEBUG lines for the high-volume, uninteresting Gameball skip paths - chiefly "integration disabled", which would otherwise fire on every profile save on a site where Gameball is switched off. Off by default; switch it on only while diagnosing why an expected sync did not happen.

When enabled, a customer registered or edited through the OCAPI/SCAPI Shop API (a headless storefront) is synced to Gameball immediately, exactly as a storefront registration is. Requires Administration > Global Preferences > Feature Switches > API hook execution to be turned on, which is off by default and cannot be detected from script - if that switch is off, this preference has no effect and the Gameball Customer Delta job is the only coverage for these customers.

When enabled, a customer created, replaced or patched through the OCAPI/SCAPI Data API (typically a CRM, OMS or middleware) is synced to Gameball inside the same request. Leave disabled for high-volume bulk upserts: the Data API hook runs inside the platform's own database transaction, so each record would hold a transaction open for the duration of a synchronous Gameball call. Coverage is not lost by leaving this off - the Gameball Customer Delta job picks those customers up within its schedule interval without holding the Data API request open.

attribute-definition.display-name: Require an Email Before Syncing a Customer
attribute-definition.description: When enabled, a customer profile with no email address is skipped by every Gameball customer sync path instead of being sent, and is recorded as gbSyncState SKIPPED. Turn this on if your Gameball workspace uses email-based channel merging: a profile with no email cannot merge and becomes a permanently orphaned Gameball record. This is a data-quality gate, not a consent gate. Default off, which preserves the previous behaviour exactly.

How the Gameball Customer Delta job finds changed profiles. LAST_MODIFIED (default) queries profiles by their last-modified date and is the cheap path. PAGED_CUSTOMER_NO pages the whole customer base in customer-number order and filters by last-modified date in code; use it only if LAST_MODIFIED fails on your instance because lastModified is not a queryable Profile attribute, which the job reports by ending with an error naming this preference. The job never switches strategy on its own.

How far back the Gameball Customer Delta job looks for modified profiles on each run. Must comfortably exceed the job's schedule interval so a skipped or failed run is recovered by the next one, and must exceed the customer search index lag (budget 1 to 1.5 hours). In PAGED_CUSTOMER_NO strategy it must also exceed the time one full pass over the customer base takes. Profiles that fall out of this window stop being retried, which is what bounds a permanently failing profile.

attribute-definition.display-name: Customer Delta Max Gameball Calls Per Run
attribute-definition.description: Upper bound on the number of Gameball customer upserts the delta job issues in a single run. Gameball caps customer POSTs at 30 per second and 360 per rolling 30 seconds account-wide, shared with every other site and every storefront call, so raising this materially requires a matching schedule change. The job ends cleanly with OK when the budget is spent; unsent profiles are picked up on the next run. A bulk customer import is a backfill in disguise - at the default of 500 per hourly run it drains at 12,000 profiles a day.

attribute-definition.display-name: Customer Delta Max Profiles Read Per Run
attribute-definition.description: Upper bound on the number of profiles the delta job reads in a single run. Only used by the PAGED_CUSTOMER_NO strategy, where it is the termination guarantee and sets how fast one full pass over the customer base completes; the LAST_MODIFIED strategy is bounded by its own query instead. Reading is cheap - this is not a Gameball call budget, and lowering it does not reduce API traffic.

attribute-definition.display-name: Allow Gameball Jobs on Non-Production Instances
attribute-definition.description: Every Gameball job refuses to run on a Sandbox, Development or Staging instance unless this is explicitly enabled, and reports that refusal as a successful run. A sandbox data refresh copies production customer and order data; without this guard a refreshed sandbox would start pushing production records into the configured Gameball workspace unattended within one job interval. Enable it only on an instance pointed at a Gameball test workspace.

Soft ceiling every Gameball job paces itself against. Gameball's published limits are 30 requests per second and 360 per rolling 30 seconds, and they are ACCOUNT-scoped: they are shared by every job, every site and every storefront call against one Gameball workspace. A multi-site merchant therefore DIVIDES this value across the sites sharing a workspace - it is never multiplied. SFCC has no sleep, so the only throttle available to a job is to stop issuing calls, which is what happens when this ceiling is reached; the run ends cleanly and the next one resumes.

Master switch for the Gameball Customer Erasure job. When OFF, right-to-be-forgotten requests are still captured and stored - nothing is lost - but no customer is deleted from Gameball. Turning it ON later drains whatever backlog is still inside the 14-day retention window. Gameball's delete is a HARD delete with no undo and no anonymize alternative, so read docs/gameball-gdpr.md before enabling it. Note that capture is deliberately NOT gated by this preference: the Gameball customer id is destroyed by the SFCC deletion itself, so it has to be recorded whether or not the drain is switched on.

How many times the Gameball Customer Erasure job calls Gameball for one customer before marking the request FAILED. The job runs every 30 minutes, so the default of 5 is roughly a 2.5-hour recovery window for a transient Gameball outage. Attempts refused by SFCC itself - an open circuit breaker or the service rate limiter - do not count, because a valve the platform closed must not burn a legal mandate's budget; a request stuck that way is instead marked FAILED once it has been PENDING for 7 days, so it cannot expire unnoticed. A FAILED request turns the job red on every subsequent run until it is resolved, and is removed by platform retention 14 days after it was first captured; it must be resolved inside that window or the mandate is lost and has to be re-issued from the Gameball dashboard. See docs/gameball-gdpr.md for the two ways to resolve one.

How long a completed erasure request is kept before the job deletes it. The row holds the shopper's Gameball customer id, which is exactly the pseudonymous identifier the erasure request existed to remove, so this is deliberately short. The Custom Object's own 14-day retention is the backstop, not the policy.

Master switch for guest order tracking. OFF by default: while it is off, any order placed without a registered customer profile (guest checkout, POS, imported and OMS-created orders) is recorded as gbTrackState=SKIPPED and earns no points, which is the behaviour of every release before this one. Turning it on makes Gameball auto-create a customer profile for each guest identity produced by gameballGuestOrderMode. Read gameballGuestOrderMode's description before enabling: guest identities cannot be re-keyed or merged afterwards by this cartridge.

How a Gameball customerId is derived for an order that has no registered customer profile. Only consulted when gameballTrackGuestOrders is on. PER_ORDER (default) mints "gb_guest_" + the SFCC order number, so every guest order becomes its own Gameball profile - deterministic, collision-free, and safe to retry, but a repeat guest never accumulates a balance. PER_EMAIL mints "gb_guest_" + the SHA-256 hex of the lower-cased, trimmed customer email joined to the site id, so the same email on the same site always resolves to one profile that accumulates points; when the order carries no usable email (POS, imported and OMS-created orders) it falls back to PER_ORDER and never derives an id from an empty value. SKIP tracks nothing, leaving guest orders SKIPPED. CHANGING THIS VALUE DOES NOT MIGRATE ALREADY-TRACKED ORDERS: their stored gbCustomerId is never rewritten, so points already earned under the old scheme stay where they are.

attribute-definition.display-name: Link Guest Orders to a Matching Customer Login
attribute-definition.description: When on (the default), an order placed without logging in is first checked against CustomerMgr.getCustomerByLogin(order email); if a customer is found the order is attributed to that registered profile with guest=false, so a shopper who forgot to sign in still earns on their real balance. CAVEAT: getCustomerByLogin matches on the LOGIN, not on the email address. On a storefront where login and email are the same string (the SFRA default) this works; on a storefront using a separate username it silently never matches and every such order falls through to gameballGuestOrderMode. Turn this off if guest checkout must never touch a registered balance. Only consulted when gameballTrackGuestOrders is on.

Outcome of syncing this order to Gameball: TRACKED (successfully sent), SKIPPED (excluded by a gating rule - integration off, replacement order, cancelled/failed status, or a guest order while gameballTrackGuestOrders is off or gameballGuestOrderMode is SKIP), or FAILED (the API call errored or returned a non-ok result).
The exact orderId value sent to Gameball's integrations/orders endpoint. Only set when gbTrackState is TRACKED. Needed so a future refund feature can replay this same id.
The exact customerId value sent to Gameball for this order. Only set when gbTrackState is TRACKED. Kept for auditability.

The error/result message from the most recent failed Gameball sync attempt on this order. Only set when gbTrackState is FAILED. Surfaced here for support visibility since there is no Gameball dashboard in this iteration.

Which rung of the identity ladder produced the gbCustomerId sent for this order: PROFILE (the order's own registered customer profile), LOGIN_MATCH (a guest order whose email resolved to an existing customer login), GUEST_PER_ORDER (a derived id from the order number) or GUEST_PER_EMAIL (a derived id from the hashed customer email). Only set when gbTrackState is TRACKED. Written for support: a GUEST_PER_ORDER value while gameballGuestOrderMode is PER_EMAIL means the order had no usable email and the empty-identifier fallback fired.

Outcome of the most recent Gameball customer upsert attempt for this profile. SYNCED - Gameball accepted the payload. FAILED - the call errored, was rejected, or was rate-limited; it is retried by the Gameball Customer Delta job for as long as the profile stays inside that job's lookback window, unless the rejection was permanent. SKIPPED - a gating rule stopped the call before it was made: this entry point is switched off, the profile has no customer number, or it has no email while Require an Email Before Syncing a Customer is on. A profile that already reads SYNCED is never relabelled SKIPPED just because an entry point is switched off, because that says nothing about whether the customer reached Gameball.

Versioned hash of the exact payload body Gameball last ACCEPTED for this profile, or last permanently rejected. Written only after a successful or permanently-rejected call, never after a retryable failure. A sync path that recomputes this hash and finds it unchanged makes no API call at all - this is the only thing stopping the hourly delta job from re-POSTing every unchanged profile in its window. Clearing this value forces a resync on the next sync of this profile, and is the supported way to push a stuck profile through again.

When a Gameball customer upsert was last ATTEMPTED for this profile, successful or not. Read gbSyncState to know the outcome. Deliberately not written when a profile was found unchanged and no call was made: writing it there would bump the profile's last-modified date on every sweep and make the sweep permanently feed itself. For the same reason it is not refreshed while an identical failure repeats from the same entry point, so on a profile stuck in FAILED it reads as when that failure was first recorded - refreshing it every attempt would hold the profile inside the delta job's lookback window forever and it would never stop being retried.
The gameballId returned by Gameball's integrations/customers 200 response. A change in this value is the only local signal that Gameball merged this profile into another one through channel merging.

Which entry point performed the most recent sync attempt: ACCOUNT_SUBMIT_REGISTRATION, ACCOUNT_SAVE_PROFILE, ORDER_CREATE_ACCOUNT, OCAPI_SHOP_POST, OCAPI_SHOP_PATCH, OCAPI_DATA_POST, OCAPI_DATA_PUT, OCAPI_DATA_PATCH, DELTA_JOB, or MERCHANT_API (merchant code calling the Gameball customer API directly). There is no Business Manager dashboard in this iteration, so this attribute is how support answers "how did this customer get to Gameball".

Compact summary of the most recent failed Gameball customer upsert, as httpStatus|gameballCode|requestId|message. Only set when gbSyncState is FAILED, and cleared on the next successful sync. requestId is the token Gameball support asks for, which is why it is a field of its own rather than buried in the message. The payload is never stored here.
